catalog.name: Airport Weather
catalog.short_description: Flight category and convective risk at departure and arrival
catalog.description: Checks visibility and ceiling at departure and arrival airports against configurable thresholds. Defaults match standard MVFR/IFR boundaries: amber when ceiling < 3000ft or visibility < 5sm, red when ceiling < 1000ft or visibility < 3sm. Also grades convective risk within the terminal radius of each airport with no coverage dilution — a deviation is not an option on climb-out or approach, so MODERATE convective risk near either airport is amber and HIGH or above is red, regardless of how small a fraction of the route it covers.

parameters.label: Amber ceiling
parameters.description: Ceiling below this triggers amber (default: MVFR boundary)

parameters.label: Amber visibility
parameters.description: Visibility below this triggers amber (default: MVFR boundary)

parameters.label: Red ceiling
parameters.description: Ceiling below this triggers red (default: IFR boundary)

parameters.label: Red visibility
parameters.description: Visibility below this triggers red (default: IFR boundary)

parameters.label: Terminal radius
parameters.description: Convective risk is checked within this distance of departure and arrival (MODERATE = amber, HIGH+ = red)

catalog.description: Checks crosswind on the best runway and wind gusts at departure and arrival airports. Uses the runway with the lowest crosswind component. Thresholds are configurable for both crosswind and gusts.

parameters.label: Crosswind (amber)
parameters.description: Crosswind threshold for amber status

parameters.label: Crosswind (red)
parameters.description: Crosswind threshold for red status

parameters.label: Gust (amber)
parameters.description: Gust threshold for amber status

parameters.label: Gust (red)
parameters.description: Gust threshold for red status

catalog.name: Density Altitude
catalog.short_description: Aircraft performance at departure and arrival
catalog.description: Computes density altitude at the departure and arrival airports from forecast temperature and QNH at the expected times, using the field elevation from the route terrain profile. High DA reduces engine power, propeller efficiency and lift — longer takeoff roll, weaker climb. Amber/red when DA exceeds the absolute thresholds (performance charts are DA-based) OR exceeds the field elevation by the delta thresholds (hot-day performance loss, relevant even at low-lying airports). Status is the worst of departure and arrival; unavailable (not green) without forecast temperature or terrain data.

parameters.label: Amber density altitude
parameters.description: Density altitude above this triggers amber

parameters.label: Red density altitude
parameters.description: Density altitude above this triggers red

parameters.label: Amber DA above field
parameters.description: DA exceeding field elevation by this triggers amber

parameters.label: Red DA above field
parameters.description: DA exceeding field elevation by this triggers red

catalog.name: Low-Level Wind Shear
catalog.short_description: Wind shear in the lowest 1000m at departure and arrival
catalog.description: Grades approach/departure wind shear from the vertical wind structure at the airports — the hazard the surface-wind advisory cannot see. Uses 0-1km bulk shear from the sounding (catches the nocturnal low-level jet: calm surface wind under an inversion with strong flow just above) and the gust factor (gust minus sustained wind). Amber when either exceeds its threshold, red on strong shear; status is the worst of departure and arrival. A surface-based inversion is reported alongside significant shear (the decoupled-flow signature). Expect airspeed fluctuations crossing the shear layer on final — consider a speed additive, or different timing (morning mixing erodes a nocturnal jet).

parameters.label: Amber 0-1km shear
parameters.description: 0-1km bulk shear above this triggers amber

parameters.label: Red 0-1km shear
parameters.description: 0-1km bulk shear above this triggers red

parameters.label: Amber gust factor
parameters.description: Gust minus sustained wind above this triggers amber (surface-level shear/turbulence)

catalog.name: VFR Feasibility
catalog.description: Composite assessment of VFR flight feasibility. Checks airport conditions (VFR/MVFR/IFR), en-route cloud clearance relative to cruise altitude, minimum cloud separation, and whether the climb-out and descent corridors near the airports are clear of BKN/OVC layers the flight would have to transit. RED indicates IFR conditions, IMC at cruise, or an OVC layer blocking climb/descent; AMBER flags marginal conditions or a BKN layer in a corridor.

parameters.label: Cloud clearance
parameters.description: Minimum vertical separation from BKN/OVC cloud layers

parameters.label: % of route in IMC (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage in IMC or marginal clearance for amber

parameters.label: % of route in IMC (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage in IMC for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

parameters.label: Terminal corridor
parameters.description: Distance from departure/arrival to check for BKN/OVC layers in the climb-out and descent path

parameters.label: Mitigation floor (AGL)
parameters.description: Minimum height above terrain for any mitigation altitude — the floor of the vertical-profile solver (#335). A lower cruise or an under-deck corridor must sit at least this far above terrain to be offered; below it there isn't safe VFR room, so the RED is genuine. Doubles as the scud-running margin beneath a deck.

parameters.label: Max reposition distance
parameters.description: Only offer an along-route 'climb after / descend before' mitigation when the VMC break is within this distance of the airport. Beyond it the deck is too extensive to thread by repositioning (you'd fly under it for most of the leg), so no mitigation is offered.

catalog.name: IFR Feasibility
catalog.description: Composite assessment of IFR flight feasibility. Checks airport conditions (LIFR triggers amber, below-minimums triggers red), en-route icing exposure percentage, and convective activity. IFR or better at airports is GREEN. Icing exceeding the threshold percentage triggers RED. The convective axis is the Convective Activity advisory's own grade — tune it there; this composite never grades convection differently.

parameters.label: Min dep ceiling
parameters.description: Minimum departure ceiling for IFR operations

parameters.label: Min arr ceiling
parameters.description: Minimum arrival ceiling for IFR approach

parameters.label: % of route with icing near cruise (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage with icing near cruise for amber

parameters.label: % of route with icing near cruise (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage with icing near cruise for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

parameters.label: Icing alt buffer
parameters.description: Icing above cruise + buffer is ignored (irrelevant altitude)

catalog.name: Approach Feasibility
catalog.short_description: Can you get in, on a runway you can also land on?
catalog.description: Joins three facts the briefing otherwise reports separately at the destination: the ceiling, the runway the wind favours, and which runways actually have a published instrument approach. A VFR destination is always green — it is visually reachable. At MVFR only the presence of an approach is checked (no approach at all is amber; alignment is not a penalty when the landing can be completed visually). At IFR/LIFR the full logic applies: green for a straight-in approach to a runway whose wind components are within limits and a ceiling clear of the estimated minima; amber for a compromise (circling required, ceiling inside the estimated minima band, or a tailwind still within limits); red only for a hard fact — no approach at all, a ceiling below even the best-case decision height, or an approach-served runway with an out-of-limits tailwind and no ceiling for circling. Decision heights are estimates shared with the alternate-requirement card, so uncertainty can only soften a grade, never harden it. If you have declared an unpublished approach at the destination in your account settings, a field with no published procedure is graded amber rather than red at IFR — never green, and never credited at LIFR, where there are no published minima to fly to. A declaration never affects alternate-minima calculations.

parameters.label: Tailwind limit
parameters.description: Tailwind on an approach-served runway above this is treated as not usable straight-in

parameters.label: Crosswind limit
parameters.description: Crosswind on an approach-served runway above this is a compromise (amber). Crosswind severity itself is graded by the Airport Wind advisory

parameters.label: Circling ceiling
parameters.description: Assumed ceiling needed to circle. Below this a misaligned approach can no longer be salvaged visually

parameters.label: Circling visibility
parameters.description: Assumed visibility needed to circle. Circling needs visual reference to the runway, so a generous ceiling in fog is not a way in

catalog.name: Winds Aloft
catalog.short_description: Headwind at cruise and trip-time impact
catalog.description: Averages the cruise-level headwind component along the route and estimates the trip-time impact versus still air, using your aircraft's cruise speed (or the flight's planned speed). Mostly informational: amber when the average headwind exceeds the threshold (fuel-planning attention), red only for extreme days. Tailwinds report the time gained. Reads winds at the evaluated cruise altitude, so the altitude table shows how the wind trade changes with level.

parameters.label: Avg headwind (amber)
parameters.description: Route-average headwind above this triggers amber

parameters.label: Avg headwind (red)
parameters.description: Route-average headwind above this triggers red

catalog.name: Icing Escape (non-FIKI)
catalog.short_description: Icing at cruise and warm-air escape viability
catalog.description: For non-FIKI aircraft. First detects icing at or below cruise altitude, then checks whether descending to warm air above terrain is viable as an escape route. The reported percentage reflects icing coverage along the route.

parameters.label: Terrain margin
parameters.description: Minimum clearance above terrain for escape

parameters.label: Tight margin
parameters.description: Freezing level below this margin above terrain triggers amber

parameters.label: Icing alt buffer
parameters.description: Icing above cruise + buffer is ignored (irrelevant altitude)

parameters.label: % of route in icing (amber)
parameters.description: Percentage of route with icing (but escape available) to trigger amber. Only applies when warm-air descent is viable everywhere along the route.

parameters.label: % of route with no escape (red)
parameters.description: Percentage of route where icing exists but descending to warm air is blocked by terrain. Any no-escape point triggers amber; exceeding this threshold escalates to red.

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

catalog.name: FIKI Icing
catalog.description: For FIKI-equipped aircraft. Evaluates icing across three flight phases: climb-out near departure, clear-air cruise proportion, and descent near arrival. FIKI can transit icing layers but should minimise exposure — thick transit layers or extended cruise in icing are concerning.

parameters.label: Proximity radius
parameters.description: Distance from origin/destination to assess climb/descent icing

parameters.label: Cruise icing buffer
parameters.description: Minimum vertical clearance from cruise altitude to nearest icing layer for clear-air cruise

parameters.label: Transit thickness amber
parameters.description: Total icing thickness during climb/descent for amber

parameters.label: Transit thickness red
parameters.description: Total icing thickness during climb/descent for red

parameters.label: % of cruise in icing (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage where cruise is not in clear air, for amber

parameters.label: % of cruise in icing (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage where cruise is not in clear air, for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

parameters.label: Severe = RED
parameters.description: Any severe icing in transit triggers RED

catalog.name: Freezing Precipitation
catalog.short_description: Freezing rain / ice pellets along the route
catalog.description: Detects freezing rain and ice pellets: a warm layer aloft over a sub-zero surface layer turns falling rain into supercooled drops that freeze on the airframe as clear ice. This happens BELOW cloud — where the in-cloud icing methods and cloud bands show nothing — and it is the one icing scenario where descending does NOT escape. Red when any model shows active freezing rain or ice pellets at any point (deliberately no coverage threshold: one transit exceeds all icing certification, FIKI included; ice pellets prove freezing rain in the layer above). Amber when a freezing-rain-shaped profile exists without active precipitation yet (primed — onset or a timing shift turns it active) over enough of the route. Unavailable (not green) on packs without precipitation data.

parameters.label: % of route with a primed profile (amber)
parameters.description: Percent of route with a freezing-rain-shaped profile (no active precip) that triggers amber

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

catalog.name: Cloud Tops
catalog.description: Checks cloud tops for layers near cruise altitude (base within clearance margin of cruise). Layers well above cruise are ignored — the pilot flies clear below them. Cloud tops near or above the flight ceiling means the pilot cannot get on top if needed.

parameters.label: Margin above tops
parameters.description: Required clearance above cloud tops

parameters.label: % of route above ceiling (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage with tops above ceiling for amber

parameters.label: % of route above ceiling (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage with tops above ceiling for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

catalog.name: VMC at Cruise
catalog.short_description: Can maintain VMC at cruise altitude
catalog.description: Checks cloud layers and NWP cloud cover at cruise altitude. BKN or OVC coverage at cruise means IMC conditions.

parameters.label: % of route in cloud at cruise (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage with BKN at cruise for amber

parameters.label: % of route overcast at cruise (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage with OVC at cruise for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

catalog.name: Convective Activity
catalog.description: Uses convective risk assessment per point. Points where tops are below cruise altitude (with clearance margin) are ignored. High/Extreme risk at any point triggers RED.

parameters.label: Min risk level
parameters.description: Minimum risk level that counts (0=NONE, 1=MARGINAL, 2=LOW, 3=MODERATE)

parameters.label: % of route with convection (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage affected for amber

parameters.label: % of route with convection (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage affected for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

parameters.label: Top clearance (ft)
parameters.description: Ignore convection whose tops are this far below cruise altitude

catalog.name: Convective Character
catalog.description: Classifies the character of route convection on a VFR-avoidability axis, independent of severity. Isolated/scattered cells in clear air (circumnavigable with see-and-avoid) grade AMBER; widespread, organized/frontal, or embedded convection (no reliable gaps, or cells hidden in cloud) grade RED. Does NOT change the Convective Activity (severity) advisory — a big cell still grades RED there regardless.

parameters.label: Min risk level
parameters.description: Minimum severity that counts as a cell (3=MODERATE, 4=HIGH)

parameters.label: Showers threshold
parameters.description: Convective precip (mm) at a point to count it as a realized cell

parameters.label: Isolated max %
parameters.description: Realized coverage at/below this is isolated

parameters.label: Scattered max %
parameters.description: Realized coverage at/below this is scattered; above is widespread

parameters.label: Organized shear (kt)
parameters.description: 0-6km shear at/above which widespread convection is organized

parameters.label: Below-base clearance (ft)
parameters.description: VMC buffer below convective bases for see-and-avoid (mirrors the overfly clearance)

parameters.label: Embedded min extent (nm)
parameters.description: Longest unbroken stretch of cells hidden in a deck at/above which the route counts as embedded

parameters.label: Embedded cruise buffer (ft)
parameters.description: Slack on "the deck contains cruise" — model levels are 1,000-2,000 ft apart near the flight levels

parameters.label: Embedded deck cover %
parameters.description: Bulk cloud cover in the band at cruise above which the layer is a stratiform deck, not the cells' own cumulus

parameters.label: Lowest cruise offered (ft AGL)
parameters.description: Terrain clearance below which the climb/descend tip will not suggest a cruise level

catalog.name: En-route Precipitation
catalog.description: Grades precipitation along the route as a visibility hazard — no model forecasts visibility at altitude, so precipitation phase and intensity are the honest proxy. Snow is the VFR killer: visibility collapses in even light snow showers and the surface phase is representative of the whole column below the melting layer, so any snow over more than a small fraction of the route is amber and widespread moderate snow is red. Moderate-or-heavier rain over a large fraction of the route is amber (reduced visibility and ceilings); light rain is noted but stays green. Freezing rain / ice pellets count toward the extent here, but their icing severity is graded by the dedicated Freezing Precipitation advisory. Unavailable (not green) on packs without precipitation data.

parameters.label: % of route in snow (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage with any snow for amber

parameters.label: % of route in moderate+ snow (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage with moderate+ snow for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

parameters.label: Rain % (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage with moderate+ rain for amber

catalog.name: Turbulence
catalog.description: Checks CAT risk layers and vertical motion at cruise altitude. Severe free-atmosphere CAT triggers RED regardless of route percentage; severe boundary-layer shear is floored at AMBER and graded by route percentage. RED via coverage requires moderate-or-worse risk — light-only coverage caps at AMBER.

parameters.label: % of route with turbulence (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage with turbulence for amber

parameters.label: % of route with moderate+ turbulence (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage with moderate-or-worse turbulence for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

parameters.label: Strong w threshold
parameters.description: Vertical velocity above this is significant

catalog.name: Mountain Wind
catalog.short_description: Wind and wave signatures near terrain
catalog.description: Evaluates wind speed near terrain tops at points where terrain exceeds a threshold, corroborated by the classical wave ingredients: a stable layer (inversion) near ridge top or a wave-like oscillating vertical-motion profile in the model. Strong wind alone is amber; very strong wind is red; and moderately strong wind WITH a wave signature is also red at a lower threshold — that combination is the rotor-day setup, not just a windy ridge.

parameters.label: Terrain threshold
parameters.description: Only evaluate points where terrain exceeds this altitude

parameters.label: Altitude margin
parameters.description: Check wind within this margin above terrain tops

parameters.label: Wind amber (kt)
parameters.description: Wind speed above terrain for amber

parameters.label: Wind red (kt)
parameters.description: Wind speed above terrain for red (severe rotor)

parameters.label: Wind red w/ signature
parameters.description: Red threshold when a wave signature (ridge-top inversion or oscillating vertical motion) is present at the same point

catalog.name: Sun
catalog.short_description: Low-sun glare on takeoff/landing + which side the sun is on
catalog.description: Informational, never a go/no-go. GREEN by default. Goes AMBER when a low sun would sit roughly down the wind-best runway on takeoff or landing (glare on the roll/flare), and — for day-VFR profiles — when the leg ends near or after sunset. It also always reports where the sun sits for most of the route — left or right (handy for deciding where to seat a passenger on the shaded side, or which window gives the better-lit shot for photos), or ahead/behind when you are flying into the sun or have it at your back. Night-capable profiles can disable the dusk AMBER via warn_near_sunset; glare AMBER always applies.

parameters.label: Glare cone half-angle
parameters.description: Sun within this many degrees of the runway heading counts as glare

parameters.label: Low-sun ceiling
parameters.description: Sun at or below this elevation counts as a low (glaring) sun

parameters.label: Warn near sunset/sunrise
parameters.description: Amber when landing near/after sunset or departing near/before sunrise (off for night-capable profiles)

parameters.label: Sunset margin
parameters.description: Treat landing within this many minutes of sunset (or departure of sunrise) as near-dark

catalog.name: Fronts (experimental)
catalog.description: This advisory looks for air-mass boundaries — which can be the signal of a front — and grades them along the route or off-track. They are graded by their intensity, the sharpness of the air-mass change, and whether they are linked to bad weather: dry air is benign, while wet or convective weather raises the grade.

parameters.label: Closing front distance
parameters.description: Flag AMBER when the nearest off-track front is closing on the route within this distance

parameters.label: Min front persistence
parameters.description: Demote a crossing to GREEN when the gradient holds in fewer than this fraction of the time-window frames (flickering = likely orographic / grid artifact, not a real front)

parameters.label: Flight-band buffer
parameters.description: A front's weather is 'relevant' when its cloud/convective top reaches cruise minus this buffer (so weather entirely below the aircraft is overflown, not graded)

parameters.label: Deep-convection height
parameters.description: A convective front reaching the flight is RED only when its tops are at least this far above cruise (deep towers); shallower build-ups are AMBER

catalog.name: Forecast Confidence
catalog.description: Re-uses the existing model divergence scores computed at each route point. POOR agreement means models disagree significantly on key variables, reducing forecast confidence.

parameters.label: Min poor variables
parameters.description: Number of variables that must be POOR to flag a waypoint

parameters.label: % of route with poor agreement (amber)
parameters.description: Route percentage with POOR agreement for amber

parameters.label: % of route with poor agreement (red)
parameters.description: Route percentage with POOR agreement for red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

catalog.name: DD vs NWP Agreement
catalog.description: Compares the sounding-derived (DD) and model-native (NWP) analysis tracks for each model on freezing level and cloud overlap.  Disagreement between these two independent derivations flags conditions the model handles poorly. Convective DD-vs-NWP divergence is reported separately by the convective advisory's inline cross-check (#283).

parameters.label: Freezing level delta
parameters.description: Absolute DD−NWP freezing level delta considered a disagreement

parameters.label: Min cloud overlap
parameters.description: Cloud layer Jaccard below this counts as disagreement

parameters.label: % of route disagreeing (amber)
parameters.description: Minimum route percentage with disagreement to flag amber

parameters.label: % of route disagreeing (red)
parameters.description: Minimum route percentage with disagreement to flag red

parameters.label: Minimum extent
parameters.description: Coverage shorter than this never promotes the grade on its own — a lone flagged point is a sliver of a long route but a large share of a short one

cloud_top.description: Checks cloud tops for layers near cruise altitude (base within clearance margin of cruise). Layers well above cruise are ignored — the pilot flies clear below them. Cloud tops near or above the flight ceiling means the pilot cannot get on top if needed.

convective_character.name: Convective Character
convective_character.description: Classifies the character of route convection on a VFR-avoidability axis, independent of severity. Isolated/scattered cells in clear air (circumnavigable with see-and-avoid) grade AMBER; widespread, organized/frontal, or embedded convection (no reliable gaps, or cells hidden in cloud) grade RED. Does NOT change the Convective Activity (severity) advisory — a big cell still grades RED there regardless.

density_altitude.cross_check_note: Cross-check notes are display-only context for discussion, not a downgrade signal. Explain the grade with them; do not argue it down.
density_altitude.name: Density Altitude
density_altitude.description: Computes density altitude at the departure and arrival airports from forecast temperature and QNH at the expected times, using the field elevation from the route terrain profile. High DA reduces engine power, propeller efficiency and lift — longer takeoff roll, weaker climb. Amber/red when DA exceeds the absolute thresholds (performance charts are DA-based) OR exceeds the field elevation by the delta thresholds (hot-day performance loss, relevant even at low-lying airports). Status is the worst of departure and arrival; unavailable (not green) without forecast temperature or terrain data.

enroute_precip.cross_check_note: Cross-check notes are display-only context for discussion, not a downgrade signal. Explain the grade with them; do not argue it down.
enroute_precip.name: En-route Precipitation
enroute_precip.description: Grades precipitation along the route as a visibility hazard — no model forecasts visibility at altitude, so precipitation phase and intensity are the honest proxy. Snow is the VFR killer: visibility collapses in even light snow showers and the surface phase is representative of the whole column below the melting layer, so any snow over more than a small fraction of the route is amber and widespread moderate snow is red. Moderate-or-heavier rain over a large fraction of the route is amber (reduced visibility and ceilings); light rain is noted but stays green. Freezing rain / ice pellets count toward the extent here, but their icing severity is graded by the dedicated Freezing Precipitation advisory. Unavailable (not green) on packs without precipitation data.

fiki_icing.cross_check_note: Cross-check notes are display-only context for discussion, not a downgrade signal. Explain the grade with them; do not argue it down.
fiki_icing.name: FIKI Icing
fiki_icing.description: For FIKI-equipped aircraft. Evaluates icing across three flight phases: climb-out near departure, clear-air cruise proportion, and descent near arrival. FIKI can transit icing layers but should minimise exposure — thick transit layers or extended cruise in icing are concerning.

flight_category.cross_check_note: Cross-check notes are display-only context for discussion, not a downgrade signal. Explain the grade with them; do not argue it down.
flight_category.name: Airport Weather
flight_category.description: Checks visibility and ceiling at departure and arrival airports against configurable thresholds. Defaults match standard MVFR/IFR boundaries: amber when ceiling < 3000ft or visibility < 5sm, red when ceiling < 1000ft or visibility < 3sm. Also grades convective risk within the terminal radius of each airport with no coverage dilution — a deviation is not an option on climb-out or approach, so MODERATE convective risk near either airport is amber and HIGH or above is red, regardless of how small a fraction of the route it covers.

freezing_precip.cross_check_note: Cross-check notes are display-only context for discussion, not a downgrade signal. Explain the grade with them; do not argue it down.
freezing_precip.name: Freezing Precipitation
freezing_precip.description: Detects freezing rain and ice pellets: a warm layer aloft over a sub-zero surface layer turns falling rain into supercooled drops that freeze on the airframe as clear ice. This happens BELOW cloud — where the in-cloud icing methods and cloud bands show nothing — and it is the one icing scenario where descending does NOT escape. Red when any model shows active freezing rain or ice pellets at any point (deliberately no coverage threshold: one transit exceeds all icing certification, FIKI included; ice pellets prove freezing rain in the layer above). Amber when a freezing-rain-shaped profile exists without active precipitation yet (primed — onset or a timing shift turns it active) over enough of the route. Unavailable (not green) on packs without precipitation data.

llws.cross_check_note: Cross-check notes are display-only context for discussion, not a downgrade signal. Explain the grade with them; do not argue it down.
llws.name: Low-Level Wind Shear
llws.description: Grades approach/departure wind shear from the vertical wind structure at the airports — the hazard the surface-wind advisory cannot see. Uses 0-1km bulk shear from the sounding (catches the nocturnal low-level jet: calm surface wind under an inversion with strong flow just above) and the gust factor (gust minus sustained wind). Amber when either exceeds its threshold, red on strong shear; status is the worst of departure and arrival. A surface-based inversion is reported alongside significant shear (the decoupled-flow signature). Expect airspeed fluctuations crossing the shear layer on final — consider a speed additive, or different timing (morning mixing erodes a nocturnal jet).

mountain_wind.cross_check_note: Cross-check notes are display-only context for discussion, not a downgrade signal. Explain the grade with them; do not argue it down.
mountain_wind.name: Mountain Wind
mountain_wind.description: Evaluates wind speed near terrain tops at points where terrain exceeds a threshold, corroborated by the classical wave ingredients: a stable layer (inversion) near ridge top or a wave-like oscillating vertical-motion profile in the model. Strong wind alone is amber; very strong wind is red; and moderately strong wind WITH a wave signature is also red at a lower threshold — that combination is the rotor-day setup, not just a windy ridge.

sun.cross_check_note: Cross-check notes are display-only context for discussion, not a downgrade signal. Explain the grade with them; do not argue it down.
sun.name: Sun
sun.description: Informational, never a go/no-go. GREEN by default. Goes AMBER when a low sun would sit roughly down the wind-best runway on takeoff or landing (glare on the roll/flare), and — for day-VFR profiles — when the leg ends near or after sunset. It also always reports where the sun sits for most of the route — left or right (handy for deciding where to seat a passenger on the shaded side, or which window gives the better-lit shot for photos), or ahead/behind when you are flying into the sun or have it at your back. Night-capable profiles can disable the dusk AMBER via warn_near_sunset; glare AMBER always applies.

turbulence.name: Turbulence
turbulence.description: Checks CAT risk layers and vertical motion at cruise altitude. Severe free-atmosphere CAT triggers RED regardless of route percentage; severe boundary-layer shear is floored at AMBER and graded by route percentage. RED via coverage requires moderate-or-worse risk — light-only coverage caps at AMBER.

digest.assessment_reason: Low overcast with drizzle and light rain at the departure end puts EGTF in IFR/LIFR with an OVC layer in the climb-out, while the rest of the route clears to VFR and Sion is CAVOK; IFR flight is workable with no icing, convection or turbulence concerns.
digest.synoptic: Under a weak, moist south-easterly to south-westerly flow, a low stratus/nimbostratus deck covers the south of England and extends to the Channel coast; it breaks up and clears south-eastward beyond BIG. REM, SAPRE and LSGS are clear to nearly clear with light winds, under building high pressure (DWD synoptic overview places High ELMAR over the Alps/Czechia, well east and south-east of the route). Convective, icing, turbulence and winds-aloft advisories are all GREEN, with CAPE nil to marginal; the DWD warm front approaches the British Isles only Monday night into Tuesday, so it is a later trend item rather than a condition for this flight.
digest.specific_concerns: Observations are consistent with or worse than the models around the departure end: EGLF IFR (BKN005, -RA), EGVO IFR (OVC005, -RADZ), EGKK IFR (3000 -DZ, BKN006), with MVFR at EGLL and along the Kent side near BIG (EGKB BKN010). TAFs carry TEMPO/PROB groups to IFR and LIFR across the corridor, so no improvement is assured at departure. VFR Feasibility is RED: LIFR at EGTF, and IMC over about 142 nm (31%, about 49 min) of the route, so departure would be IMC. Radar shows an observed echo of 45 dBZ about 15 NM SE of EGTF and moderate precipitation east of EGTF, i.e. on the initial track toward BIG; no lightning observed. En-route precipitation is light over about 26% of the route. Cloud tops reach 12,609 ft in the forecast, with an observed cloud top near FL465 about 142 NM along the route (multi-layer high cloud). Beyond BIG the route clears: REM and SAPRE are VFR/CAVOK, and LSGS is CAVOK with variable winds 2 kt and a crosswind of 2 kt. Low sun (~10° up) is nearly down RWY 25 on landing at LSGS, so expect glare on the flare. Climbing or descending (4,000 ft) does not change the advisory picture. ECMWF alone is slightly more pessimistic on fronts (AMBER), GFS alone on IFR feasibility and VMC at cruise (31% affected).
digest.trend: Consistent with the previous digest, which was also AMBER: stratus at the departure end clearing to the south-east, with the destination clear. Observations confirm the picture, with the departure end IFR/LIFR and the south-east clear, and the TAFs have not yet shown a firm improvement. Models disagree on cloud cover at REM, but observed CAVOK nearby supports the clear solution.
digest.watch_items: 1) EGTF and nearby METAR/TAF trends: any improvement in ceiling and visibility, or conversely LIFR TEMPOs for drizzle and stratus. 2) The area of moderate precipitation and 45 dBZ echo SE/E of EGTF, whether it moves across the track toward BIG. 3) The warm front and the secondary trough approaching the British Isles Monday night into Tuesday, bringing multi-layered cloud and light rain from the west and northwest, a concern for any later or return flight. 4) Sun glare on the approach to RWY 25 at LSGS late in the day.
